overview: Tapestry, Inc. is a global house of accessible-luxury accessories and lifestyle brands, built around Coach and kate spade new york. The Company designs, markets and sells handbags, accessories, footwear and lifestyle products through directly-operated stores and e-commerce (DTC, ~87% of sales), wholesale department stores and specialty retailers (~12%), and brand licensing (~1%). Tapestry operates globally with roughly 59% of net sales from North America and the balance from Greater China, other Asia, Europe and the Middle East, following the August 2025 divestiture of Stuart Weitzman and the 2024 collapse of its attempted acquisition of Capri Holdings (Michael Kors' parent).

business_model.summary: Tapestry earns the large majority of revenue from Coach, a premium/'accessible luxury' handbag and accessories brand that has reaccelerated growth under a 2028 'Amplify' strategy, while Kate Spade is a smaller, currently shrinking lifestyle brand undergoing a reset. Revenue is transactional (point-of-sale product sales), not subscription-based, but repeat/brand-loyal purchasing and a growing DTC mix give it more recurring-like characteristics than typical apparel retail. Customers are overwhelmingly B2C consumers, supplemented by B2B wholesale relationships with department stores and licensing partners (eyewear, watches, fragrance, tech accessories) who pay royalties on branded goods.
business_model.customer_type: Primarily B2C consumers (premium/aspirational accessories shoppers, with a growing Gen Z focus), plus B2B wholesale department-store and licensing relationships
business_model.geographic_mix: North America ~59%, Greater China ~20%, Other Asia (Japan, Australia, South Korea, etc.) ~12%, Other (Europe, Middle East, licensing royalties) ~10% (Q1 FY2027 disaggregation)

competitive_position.market_position: Leading player in the 'accessible/aspirational luxury' handbag segment via Coach (targeting the roughly $200-$500 price band), with Kate Spade positioned in colorful, feminine lifestyle accessories; Coach alone is pursuing a stated ambition to become a $10 billion brand

moat_factors.description: Coach (founded 1941) and kate spade new york (1993) carry decades of brand equity and strong consumer recognition in North America and increasingly in Greater China
Dedicated brand design teams plus investment in data analytics, AI and merchandising tools support faster response to shifting consumer preferences

Long-standing 'better brand' manufacturing partnerships across Vietnam, Cambodia, the Philippines, India and Bangladesh support quality control and cost competitiveness, though no single vendor provides 10%+ of inventory, limiting single-point risk
Multi-year licensing deals (Luxottica eyewear, Movado watches, Interparfums fragrance, etc.) extend brand reach into adjacent categories at low capital cost
Coach has pulled back on promotional activity and introduced full-price collection merchandise into outlet stores, supporting gross margin expansion (77.8% in FY2026)

weaknesses: Heavy and growing concentration in a single brand (Coach = 86.4% of FY2026 net sales), amplifying the impact of any misstep in design, marketing or leadership

Kate Spade is now a drag rather than a complement: net sales down 10.2% in FY2026 and down again in Q1 FY2027, with a swing to an operating loss following an $854.8 million FY2025 goodwill/brand impairment
Low switching costs and intense competition in a fashion/trend-driven category where consumer tastes can shift quickly

History of a large, costly, ultimately failed strategic bet (the blocked $8.5 billion Capri Holdings acquisition), which consumed management time and required redeeming $6 billion of acquisition financing at a loss
Wholesale channel (~12% of sales) remains exposed to ongoing department-store consolidation and promotional pressure

growth_drivers: 'Amplify' 2028 growth strategy (launched Q1 FY2026): new customer acquisition focused on Gen Z, product innovation in handbags/leathergoods with footwear expansion, and accelerated growth in Greater China and Europe
Coach's reduced-discounting, full-price strategy and ~50% increase in marketing spend driving brand heat and margin expansion
International growth, particularly reacceleration in Greater China and Europe, diversifying away from a maturing North America base
Continued digital/e-commerce and omnichannel investment, plus use of AI/machine learning in merchandising, personalization and pricing
Large capital return program (~$2.0 billion planned in FY2027 via buybacks and dividends) mechanically boosting EPS as share count shrinks

Simplified two-brand portfolio (post Stuart Weitzman divestiture and terminated Capri deal) freeing management and capital to focus on Coach's stated $10 billion ambition, with M&A optionality preserved for future opportunistic deals

business.description: Coach generates 86%+ of net sales; any slowdown in Coach demand, a design misstep, or loss of key creative/marketing talent would disproportionately hit consolidated results
Kate Spade sales have declined for multiple consecutive periods and swung to an operating loss after a large brand/goodwill impairment in FY2025; there is no assurance the brand reset will succeed

business.risk: Intense competition and changing consumer preferences
business.description: Competes against both aspirational mass brands and true luxury houses; rapid fashion-trend shifts and the rise of AI shopping assistants could erode share if Tapestry fails to anticipate changes
Department-store restructurings, bankruptcies and ownership changes could reduce wholesale distribution points (~12% of sales)
Brand dilution from counterfeit goods, compounded by AI tools complicating enforcement of intellectual property

financial.description: ~$2.38 billion of consolidated debt as of June 27, 2026, with a maximum net leverage covenant of 4.00x (4.50x post-material-acquisition) under the revolving credit facility; breach would trigger cross-default on senior notes
Significant international sales and intercompany transactions create translation and transaction FX risk, only partially hedged
~$2.0 billion of planned FY2027 buybacks/dividends require continued strong free cash flow; any downturn could force a choice between capital returns and balance-sheet flexibility
OECD Pillar Two GloBE global minimum tax rules began negatively affecting the effective tax rate starting in FY2026

regulatory.description: FY2026 gross margin was hurt ~130bps by tariffs; the Supreme Court invalidated IEEPA tariffs (refunds still being processed), a subsequent Section 122 10% global tariff was ruled invalid and is under appeal, and new Section 301 tariffs of 10-12.5% took effect in July 2026 on goods from key manufacturing countries (Vietnam, Cambodia, Philippines, India, Bangladesh)
Putative securities class actions alleging misrepresentations about the terminated Capri merger remain pending (motion to dismiss the amended complaint filed June 2026)
Evolving global AI and data-privacy rules (EU AI Act, U.S. state privacy laws) could raise compliance costs and constrain AI-driven personalization/marketing initiatives
The FTC's successful 2024 injunction against the Capri acquisition signals continued antitrust scrutiny of further large M&A in the sector

macro.description: Handbags/accessories are discretionary purchases that are pressured by inflation, high interest rates, unemployment and weak consumer confidence

macro.risk: China consumer sentiment and tourism patterns
macro.description: Greater China is a key growth market (~20% of Q1 FY2027 sales); shifts in Chinese consumer spending, local competition or geopolitical tension with the U.S. could slow growth
The Middle East conflict and broader geopolitical uncertainty have modestly affected supply chains and energy costs, though direct Tapestry exposure to the region is minimal
Concentration of manufacturing in Vietnam, Cambodia, the Philippines, India and Bangladesh exposes the Company to shipping, labor and input-cost volatility

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global accessible/aspirational-luxury handbags and accessories category is growing moderately, with brands like Coach capturing demand migrating both up from mass-market and down from ultra-luxury houses amid an uncertain consumer backdrop; true luxury conglomerates (LVMH, Kering) have seen softer demand, creating relative share opportunity for well-positioned 'affordable luxury' players
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - handbags and accessories are consumer-discretionary purchases, though lower price points relative to true luxury provide some 'lipstick effect' resilience in downturns
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct exposure given mostly fixed-rate senior notes, but moderate indirect sensitivity through consumer spending power and the cost of any incremental borrowing/commercial paper
key_input_costs: Manufacturing labor costs in Vietnam, Cambodia, the Philippines, India and Bangladesh

recent_developments.event: Completed sale of the Stuart Weitzman business to Caleres, Inc. for a final price of $109.1 million, leaving Coach and Kate Spade as the Company's only two reportable segments
Introduced the 2028 'Amplify' growth strategy focused on Gen Z acquisition, product innovation, global expansion (Greater China/Europe) and culture
Board authorized a new $3.0 billion share repurchase program (the '2026 Share Repurchase Program'), replacing the 2022 program's $561.7 million remaining authorization
Q2 FY2026 results beat expectations with Coach revenue up ~25%; shares hit then-record highs (~$143-$162 over the following weeks)
U.S. Supreme Court ruled IEEPA tariffs invalid; Tapestry pursued and largely collected an estimated $114.7-115 million refund on previously paid tariffs through Q1 FY2027

U.S. Administration imposed new Section 301 tariffs of 10%-12.5% on imports from several of Tapestry's key manufacturing countries, following expiration of a temporary Section 122 global tariff that was separately ruled invalid and is under appeal
Reported record fiscal 2026 net sales of $8.00 billion (+14.2%) and net income of $1.53 billion, driven by Coach net sales growth of 23.5%, while Kate Spade net sales fell 10.2%

Q1 FY2027 results beat estimates (adjusted diluted EPS of $1.82 vs. ~$1.56 consensus; net sales +11.1% to $1.89 billion); raised FY2027 EPS guidance to $8.25-$8.35 and revenue guidance to $8.5-$8.6 billion, while increasing planned FY2027 share buybacks by $350 million to $1.7 billion

At least one major sell-side firm (BofA Securities) downgraded TPR citing valuation concerns after the stock's strong 2026 run, while other firms (e.g., UBS) maintained high price targets (up to $230)

items.notes: Up from a prior range of approximately $8.4-$8.5 billion, reflecting continued Coach strength
Raised from $7.80-$7.90; above the prior analyst consensus of ~$7.96
Slightly above analyst consensus of ~$3.02 at the time of guidance
Includes dividends and buybacks; planned share repurchases increased by $350 million to $1.7 billion for the year; ~$700 million already returned in Q1 FY2027

items.metric: Capital expenditures and cloud computing costs
items.notes: Consistent with recent years' spend; includes investment in the Ohio-to-Pennsylvania distribution network transition

guidance.management_commentary: Management described Q1 FY2027 growth as broad-based across customer cohorts and geographies for Coach, with North America, Greater China and Europe all contributing to DTC growth. Kate Spade remains a near-term drag, with management acknowledging continued sales pressure and pointing to a possible turnaround in the back half of fiscal 2027 rather than an immediate fix. Management continues to flag an uncertain U.S. tariff and trade-policy environment as an ongoing watch item even as recent IEEPA refunds provided a one-time benefit.

bull_case: Coach's Amplify strategy has produced a genuine brand resurgence (net sales +23.5% in FY2026, +16.1% in Q1 FY2027) with broad-based growth across cohorts and geographies, alongside gross margin expansion from reduced discounting
A now-simplified two-brand portfolio, free of the distracting and costly Capri pursuit, lets management focus capital and attention on Coach's stated ambition to become a $10 billion brand

Aggressive, raised capital return program (~$2.0 billion planned in FY2027, including a larger $1.7 billion buyback) directly shrinks share count and supports further EPS growth independent of top-line momentum
International growth is reaccelerating, particularly in Greater China and Europe, diversifying the business beyond a maturing North American base
Management has repeatedly beaten and raised guidance through FY2026 and into Q1 FY2027, suggesting underlying momentum and conservative initial targets
bear_case: Kate Spade's turnaround has not materialized: sales have declined for multiple consecutive quarters, the brand swung to an operating loss, and it followed an $854.8 million FY2025 impairment, raising doubts about the Company's ability to run a credible two-brand portfolio
Extreme and growing dependence on a single brand (Coach at 86%+ of sales) concentrates fashion-cycle and execution risk; any stumble in design, marketing or Gen Z appeal would hit the whole company

Unresolved U.S. tariff and trade-policy uncertainty (new Section 301 tariffs of 10-12.5% from July 2026, appeals pending on other tariff actions) threatens further gross margin pressure given concentrated sourcing in Vietnam, Cambodia, the Philippines, India and Bangladesh

The stock's strong run (reportedly up roughly 85% over the trailing year into early 2026, before further gains) has already priced in much of the Coach turnaround, prompting at least one major sell-side downgrade on valuation grounds; multiple contraction is a risk if Coach momentum decelerates (management itself has flagged slowing North America growth and a weaker Q2 outlook for Kate Spade)

Residual overhang from the failed, highly public Capri Holdings acquisition attempt (unresolved securities class-action litigation, demonstrated execution/regulatory risk in pursuing large M&A) could resurface or recur if management pursues future deals
